transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Um... I guess I just... haven't been doing great lately. 

I keep having these thoughts that... that I've completely let my family down. We took on this mortgage, and... I don't know. It just feels like a mistake. And then at work—I wait tables—if I make even a really small mistake, it just... it feels like proof that I'm useless. Like I just deserve whatever bad things happen to me. 

So... yeah. I guess that's why I'm here.
Have you been feeling this way for most of the last two years, or is this a shift from how you were feeling a few months ago?

Um... I guess it's been most of that time. Not quite two years, maybe... like a year and eight months? 

It pretty much started after I took on the mortgage for the condo. So... yeah. It's been a while.
During this period of nearly two years, have there been any stretches of at least two weeks where your mood and energy were so low that you couldn't function at work or take care of yourself at all?

Um... I don't know about not functioning at all. I still go to work. But... yeah, most days there's just... this heavy, empty feeling in my chest. 

I just kind of go through the motions. I carry the plates, I smile at the customers... but it's just because I'm supposed to. Not because I actually feel anything good. It's just... heavy.
Have there ever been any periods of at least two weeks where you felt so down that you were completely unable to do your job or take care of your basic needs?

Um... I haven't completely stopped going to work. But... it's gotten harder. 

I almost missed a few shifts recently. And... I messed up some of the mortgage paperwork. At work, doing the POS reports and keeping track of inventory... it's just taking more out of me. I keep worrying I'm going to get fired, and then... I don't know what I'd do about the condo. 

I guess I've also been... keeping to myself more. My brother and some people at work have said something about it. That I seem different. But... I'm still doing things. Mostly.

Have there been any specific periods of at least two weeks where your mood felt significantly worse than your usual 'heavy' baseline, perhaps where you felt completely unable to get out of bed or handle even basic tasks?

Um... yeah, I guess so. There are times when it gets worse than just heavy. Where I feel... I don't know, really down. And just... guilty about things. 

If I had to add up all those really bad stretches together... it's probably been about a year and two months out of this whole time.
During those really bad stretches when you felt much worse than your usual baseline, did you notice a significant change in your appetite or your sleep patterns?

Um... I don't know about sleep. But my eating is... it's all over the place. 

Some weeks I barely touch the staff meal at the restaurant. I just don't want it. But then... other nights I get back to the condo and just eat whatever's in the kitchen. Just trying to feel... settled, I guess.

During those really bad stretches you mentioned, did you experience any two-week periods where you felt so exhausted or slowed down that you were physically unable to get out of bed or perform your daily tasks?

Um... I don't know about not being able to get out of bed. But... people at work have said things. 

Like... sometimes I guess I pace around a lot. Just checking the same tables... looking at the same receipts over and over. And then other times... I don't know, they say I just get really slow. Like it takes me forever just to grab menus or... walk over to the POS system. I don't really notice it, but... they do.
During those 'really bad' stretches you mentioned, did you feel a complete loss of interest or pleasure in almost all of the activities you usually enjoy?
Um... I don't know. I guess I don't really have many activities I enjoy anyway. I just... go to work and come home. So I haven't really noticed a difference with that.

Looking back at the last year and eight months, was there ever a clear, distinct period of at least two weeks where you felt significantly worse than your usual 'heavy' baseline, specifically involving a clear loss of interest in things or feeling like you had almost no energy at all?

I mean... I don't really track it like that. It all just kind of runs together. And like I said, I don't really do much anyway besides work, so... I don't know. I can't really point to a specific two weeks where it was... worse.
Have there ever been any periods in your life, lasting at least a few days, where you felt unusually energetic, talkative, or like your mind was racing, even if it felt good at the time?
No, not really. I'm usually just... tired. I don't get bursts of energy or anything like that.
